disease_name: Anthracnose / Die-back and Ripe Fruit Rot
affected_plant_part: Twigs, branches, ripe red and green fruits
symptoms: Die-back of tender twigs from tip downwards; twigs turn white to grayish straw-colored with black acervuli dots. On fruits, circular sunken lesions with concentric rings of salmon-pink/black fruiting bodies; diseased fruits shrivel, bleach, and drop prematurely.
favorable_conditions: Warm and humid weather, temperatures of 28-30°C, RH >80%, post-monsoon rain showers during fruiting.
risk_factors: Overhead irrigation, unseasonal showers, high plant density, infected seeds.
prevention: Seed treatment with Thiram or Captan @ 3g/kg seed or Trichoderma viride @ 4g/kg. Destroy infected plant debris after harvest.
management: Foliar spray of Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1.0ml/L or Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1.0ml/L or Copper Oxychloride 50 WP @ 2.5g/L. Spray at flowering and repeat at 15-day intervals during fruit maturation.

symptoms: Upward curling of leaf margins, leaf thickening, vein clearing, brittle puckered leaves, shortening of petioles, bushy rosette stunted appearance. Severe flower dropping, deformed small fruits.
favorable_conditions: Warm dry conditions (25-35°C), high population of whiteflies.
risk_factors: Continuous cropping of solanaceous crops, weed reservoirs around field borders, dry weather spells.
prevention: Border cropping with 3 rows of Maize or Jowar. Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps/acre). Use tolerant varieties.
management: Uproot and bury severely infected plants. Spray vector-control insecticides: Spiromesifen 22.9% SC @ 1.0ml/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1.25g/L or Imidacloprid 17.8% SL @ 0.3ml/L. Alternate with neem oil 10,000 ppm @ 2ml/L.

symptoms: Small circular spots with white or bleached grayish centers surrounded by prominent dark brown margins resembling a frog's eye. Heavy infections cause complete leaf yellowing and severe defoliation, exposing fruits to sunscald.
favorable_conditions: High humidity (>85%), warm temperatures (25-30°C), frequent rains or overhead watering.
risk_factors: Dense foliage, splashing rainwater from bare soil, nutrient-stressed plants.
prevention: Ensure wide spacing, mulch with organic material, avoid overhead splashing.
management: Spray Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Carbendazim 12% + Mancozeb 63% WP (Saaf) @ 2.0g/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1.0ml/L upon spotting initial leaf lesions.
